mots.sens: The name 'Moses' means 'drawn out of the waters,' referring to his rescue by Pharaoh's daughter. Moses is a central figure in the history of Israel, representing the intermediary between God and His people. His role as a leader and prophet is crucial for the revelation of divine law and the spiritual guidance of the Israelites.

The term 'assembly' refers to a group of people gathered for a common purpose, often in reference to the people of God. In this context, it emphasizes the importance of community in fulfilling divine commands. Spiritually, it reminds us that faith is lived out collectively and that each member has a role to play in God's plan.

The verb 'to command' implies a formal and authoritative instruction given by God. This word underscores the nature of divine authority and the obligation of believers to respond to these commandments. Spiritually, it reminds us that obedience to God's word is essential for living in accordance with His will.

The term 'Lord' (or 'God') is used to refer to the all-powerful creator, the one who made a covenant with Israel. This word evokes God's sovereignty and faithfulness to His people. In this verse, it highlights the importance of recognizing divine authority in the instructions given to Moses.

1.epoque: This passage takes place during the Exodus period, when the Israelites have left Egypt and are heading toward the Promised Land under Moses' leadership.
1.passage: In this chapter, Moses reminds the Israelites of God's commandments regarding the construction of the tabernacle, a place of meeting between God and His people, emphasizing the importance of the divine presence among them.
1.culture: In Hebrew culture, the assembly is a fundamental element of community and religious life. The instructions given by Moses to the entire people show the importance of collective commitment to divine orders.
1.interpretation: This verse highlights Moses' authority as God's spokesperson, as well as the importance of the collective obedience of the Israelites. It reminds us that the community of believers must respond together to God's calls.
1.commentaire: This passage teaches us that God has a specific plan for His people and that everyone has a role to play in fulfilling that plan. As a community of believers, we must be attentive to divine instructions and respond with faith and obedience, knowing that our collective commitment is essential for living out God's will.

mots.sens: The word 'Shabbat' means 'rest' or 'cessation.' It is derived from the Hebrew root 'שׁבַת' which evokes the idea of stopping or resting. In the biblical context, the Sabbath is instituted as a holy day, reserved for the Lord, marking a separation between daily work and worship. Theologically, it reminds us of the importance of divine rest and the sanctification of time.

The term 'Qadosh' means 'holy' or 'consecrated.' It is often used to describe what is set apart for God. In this verse, the Sabbath is referred to as a 'holy thing,' emphasizing its sacred character and the importance of observing this day as a time dedicated to communion with God. It reminds us that our time should also be devoted to spiritual activities.

The word 'Avodah' means 'work' or 'service.' It is often used to refer to physical labor or religious service. In this context, it emphasizes the distinction between daily work and Sabbath rest, reminding us that the Sabbath is a time when we abstain from all forms of work to focus on God. It teaches us the importance of devotion and spiritual rest.

The word 'Mavet' means 'death.' In this verse, it evokes the seriousness of disobedience to the divine institution of the Sabbath. The mention of a death penalty for those who violate this commandment underscores the importance of respecting God's laws and the spiritual and communal consequences of our actions. It reminds us that God's holiness requires a serious respect for His commandments.

2.epoque: This passage takes place in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, recently freed from slavery in Egypt, receive God's laws at Mount Sinai.
2.passage: Exodus 35 is part of the instructions given by God regarding the construction of the tabernacle and worship, while emphasizing the importance of the Sabbath as a day of rest and sanctification.
2.culture: In Hebrew culture, the Sabbath is a fundamental day, marked by rituals and practices that reinforce community and spiritual identity. It is a time for rest, prayer, and family.
2.interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of the Sabbath as a gift from God for rest and spiritual regeneration. It reminds us that time dedicated to God is essential for our physical and spiritual well-being.
2.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of taking time to rest and dedicate ourselves to God. In our modern world, it is easy to neglect spiritual rest, but God calls us to sanctify moments for Him. By observing the Sabbath, we honor God and renew our commitment to Him.

mots.sens: The word 'שָׁבַת' (Shabbat) means 'to cease' or 'to rest.' It is derived from the root 'שָׁבַת,' which evokes the idea of stopping, detaching from daily work. In the biblical context, the Shabbat is a day of rest instituted by God, where man is called to remember creation and to devote himself to communion with the Lord. Spiritually, it represents a time of regeneration and reflection on the relationship with God.

The term 'אֵש' (Esh) denotes fire, an element that is both purifying and destructive. In the Old Testament, fire is often associated with the presence of God, as in the burning bush. However, here, the prohibition against lighting a fire on the Sabbath underscores the importance of sanctifying this day, where man should focus on his relationship with God rather than material concerns.

The word 'מָשָׁל' (Mishkan) refers to the 'dwelling' or 'tabernacle,' the place of divine presence among the people of Israel. This term evokes the idea of sanctuary and separation from the profane. In the context of the Sabbath, it reminds believers that their lives should be a space of encounter with God, where daily activities should not interfere with worship and devotion.

3.epoque: This verse comes from a time when the Israelites, recently freed from slavery in Egypt, were receiving instructions on how to live as God's people in the desert.
3.passage: In Exodus 35, the people are called to contribute to the construction of the tabernacle, and the instructions regarding the Sabbath emphasize the importance of respecting this day of rest while engaging in sacred works.
3.culture: In Hebrew culture, the Sabbath is a day of rest and sanctification, where daily activities are suspended to focus on God and community. It reflects a view of time where each day is dedicated to God.
3.interpretation: The prohibition against lighting a fire on the Sabbath symbolizes the necessity of turning away from profane activities to dedicate oneself to spirituality. It reminds believers of the importance of sanctifying time and devotion to God.
3.commentaire: This verse teaches us that the Sabbath is a divine gift, a moment of rest and spiritual renewal. As Christians, we are called to honor this principle of rest, distancing ourselves from the distractions of the world to draw closer to God. It invites us to reflect on our own practices of rest and to seek ways to place God at the center of our daily lives.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to do' or 'to act'. It evokes the idea of a concrete and intentional action, often related to creation or the fulfillment of a task. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the importance of obedience to the divine command, indicating that the actions of the Israelites must align with God's commandments, which is fundamental to their relationship with Him.

This term translates to 'commandment' or 'precept'. It represents a divine directive that believers are called to follow. In this verse, it is essential to understand that God's instructions are not merely suggestions, but orders that require an active response from His people, thus highlighting the importance of submission to divine will.

This word designates 'God' and is often used to express divine majesty and power. In the context of this verse, it reminds the Israelites that it is the Lord, the Creator, who gives orders and instructions. This reinforces the idea that their obedience is a response to God's supreme authority, which is fundamental to their identity as a chosen people.

4.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, recently freed from slavery in Egypt, receive instructions to build the tabernacle, a symbol of God's presence among them.
4.passage: Moses, as leader and mediator between God and the people, announces the commandments of the Lord regarding the construction of the tabernacle and the collection of necessary offerings, emphasizing the importance of collective obedience.
4.culture: In Israelite culture, obedience to God's commandments was essential for maintaining a right relationship with Him. The tabernacle represented not only a place of worship but also a space where the people could encounter God in a tangible way.
4.interpretation: This verse illustrates the importance of divine communication through intermediaries like Moses. It reminds believers that God's instructions must be taken seriously and put into practice, as they are essential for living in accordance with His will.
4.commentaire: This passage teaches us that obedience to the word of God is crucial for our spiritual life. As a community of believers, we are called to listen and act according to divine directives, recognizing that each act of faith contributes to the building of our relationship with God. May our response be a commitment to live according to His commandments, just as the Israelites were called to do.

mots.sens: This word means 'to give voluntarily' or 'to offer willingly'. It evokes the idea of generosity that comes not from obligation, but from a deep desire to contribute. The root of this term emphasizes the importance of the attitude of the heart in the act of giving, which is fundamental in the relationship between man and God.

The term 'lêb' designates the heart, not only as a physical organ but also as the center of emotions, will, and thought. In the Bible, the heart is often the seat of spiritual and ethical motivations. Thus, the fact that the offering must come from a 'willing heart' underscores the importance of inner disposition in serving God.

This word translates to 'offering' or 'gift', and it specifically designates a contribution made to God for a sacred purpose. It is often used in the context of offerings for the tabernacle or the temple. The notion of offering in this verse implies an active and voluntary participation of the faithful in God's work.

The word 'El' means 'God' and is often used to denote divine power. In the context of this verse, it reminds donors that their offerings are intended for the Lord, thus highlighting the sacred nature of the act of giving. This illuminates the relationship between the creator and His creation, where the offering is a response to God's goodness.

5.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, a time when the Israelites, recently freed from slavery in Egypt, receive instructions to build the tabernacle, a symbol of God's presence among them.
5.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses calls the people to contribute to the construction of the tabernacle. This chapter emphasizes the necessity of offering voluntarily and with a willing heart, thus preparing the people to actively participate in God's work.
5.culture: In Israelite culture, offerings were an integral part of worship and community life. They expressed gratitude to God and recognition of His provision, while also strengthening the bond among community members.
5.interpretation: This verse teaches us that God desires offerings that come from a sincere and generous heart. The emphasis is on inner disposition rather than the quantity of gifts, highlighting that God looks at the heart rather than outward appearance.
5.commentaire: This passage reminds us that our contribution to God's work must be motivated by an authentic desire to serve and glorify the Lord. By offering what we have, we participate in His plan and demonstrate our trust in His provision. May our hearts always be willing to give, not only material goods but also our time and love for others.

mots.sens: This word designates a red dye, often associated with the color crimson. It is derived from the root 'tola', which means 'worm', a reference to the insect from which the pigment was extracted. Spiritually, the crimson color symbolizes sacrifice and blood, evoking the sacrifice of Christ and the redemption of sins.

This term refers to a type of fine fabric, often linen, used in sacred contexts. It is linked to the idea of purity and holiness, as linen is considered a pure material. From a theological perspective, this reminds us of the importance of purity in our approach to God.

This word designates wool, often used for making garments. Wool is associated with softness and protection. Spiritually, this evokes the gentleness of Christ, our shepherd, who covers and protects us from our iniquities.

This word, meaning 'worm' or 'insect', is related to the crimson dye. It symbolizes fragility and mortality, but also the process of transformation. Theologically, this reminds us that through Christ's death, we are transformed and purified.

6.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, freshly freed from Egyptian slavery, receive instructions for the construction of the Tabernacle, a symbol of God's presence among them.
6.passage: Exodus 35 describes the necessary contributions for the construction of the Tabernacle. This chapter emphasizes the importance of community commitment and generosity in the worship of God.
6.culture: In Israelite culture, the colors and materials used in the Tabernacle had profound significance, symbolizing beauty, purity, and holiness. The artisans were called to give their best to honor God.
6.interpretation: This verse reminds us that worshiping God requires both material and spiritual sacrifices. The materials mentioned are symbols of the richness and diversity of God's creation, which should be used for His glory.
6.commentaire: As believers, we are called to offer our talents and resources for the service of God. Like the Israelites, we must be ready to give our best for God's work, knowing that every contribution, big or small, has value in His kingdom.

mots.sens: This word refers to 'skin' or 'hide', often used to denote materials derived from animals. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the importance of material offerings for the construction of the tabernacle, representing the necessity of sacrificing goods for the service of God. The dyed ram's skin also evokes sacrifice and blood, symbolizing redemption and atonement.

This term refers to the skin of a dolphin or a marine animal, often interpreted as a precious and rare material. Its use in the tabernacle symbolizes protection and beauty, reminding us that God uses what is precious for His glory. It can also represent the diversity of gifts and resources that God provides for the edification of His people.

This word designates acacia wood, a durable and resilient material often used for construction. In the context of the tabernacle, it symbolizes the solidity and permanence of God's presence among His people. The acacia wood also recalls the idea of humanity, as the tree is a creation of God, and underscores the necessity of a solid foundation for worship.

7.epoque: This passage takes place during the Exodus, as the Israelites, freed from slavery in Egypt, prepare to establish a place of worship in the midst of the desert.
7.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses calls the people to contribute to the construction of the tabernacle, a sacred space where God will dwell among them. This chapter emphasizes the importance of collective participation and voluntary offering for the divine mission.
7.culture: In the ancient cultural context, material offerings were essential for establishing places of worship. The materials mentioned here, such as skins and wood, testify to the value placed on beauty and quality in the service of God.
7.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse teaches us that God desires us to offer Him what is precious to us. The materials chosen for the tabernacle symbolize not only sacrifice but also the beauty and dignity we should accord to our worship.
7.commentaire: This passage reminds us that our commitment to God must be manifested through concrete actions and offerings of our time, resources, and talents. By participating in God's work, we contribute to the building of His kingdom on earth while honoring His presence among us.

mots.sens: The word 'shemen' refers to oil, which in Hebrew culture is often associated with blessing and the presence of God. This oil is used for anointing, symbolizing separation for sacred service. In this verse, it is specifically intended for the lampstand, representing the divine light that illuminates the believer's path.

The term 'minḥah' refers to an offering, often of flour or aromatic elements, presented to God. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the importance of giving what is precious to honor God. This evokes an attitude of heart in service and worship, where each offering is an act of devotion.

The word 'b'samim' means spices or perfumes, used to create an atmosphere of holiness in worship. These fragrant substances are a symbol of the prayers and worship that rise to God, evoking the sweetness of communion with Him. Their use in the tabernacle underscores the beauty and grandeur of divine worship.

8.epoque: This passage takes place in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, freed from slavery in Egypt, receive specific instructions for the construction of the tabernacle, a symbol of God's presence among them.
8.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses calls the people to contribute to the construction of the tabernacle. This chapter emphasizes the importance of community participation and voluntary offering for the service of God.
8.culture: In Hebrew culture, oil, spices, and offerings were symbols of devotion and sacrifice. They represented not only material elements but also spiritual expressions of commitment to God.
8.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse reminds us that our worship should be accompanied by offerings that honor God. The oil for the lampstand symbolizes the light of Christ in our lives, while the spices evoke the sweetness of our worship and prayers.
8.commentaire: This passage invites us to reflect on our own commitment to God and how we offer our time, resources, and worship. By bringing our 'best things' to God, we participate in the building of His kingdom and the flourishing of our faith community.

mots.sens: The term 'אֹנִYX' (onyx) refers to a precious stone, often used in ornaments. In the biblical context, onyx symbolizes beauty and value, also representing divine perfection. This stone, with its distinct stripes, evokes the diversity and harmony of God's creation, highlighting the importance of beauty in worship and God's presence among His people.

The word 'חֹשֶן' (breastplate) refers to an essential element of the priestly garment, bearing the precious stones representing the tribes of Israel. This breastplate symbolizes mediation between God and His people, indicating that the priest carries the names of the tribes before God. Spiritually, this reminds us that God cares for each individual and their representation in worship.

9.epoque: This passage takes place in the context of the Exodus, as the Israelites, having come out of Egypt, receive instructions for the construction of the tabernacle and priestly garments.
9.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses reminds the people of the instructions given by God for the construction of the tabernacle, emphasizing the importance of the precious materials needed to glorify divine service.
9.culture: In ancient culture, precious stones were not only symbols of wealth but also important spiritual elements, often associated with deities and protection.
9.interpretation: The instruction regarding the onyx stones and others for the ephod and breastplate underscores the importance of beauty and value in the worship of God. It reminds us that our worship should be done with excellence, considering the greatness of God.
9.commentaire: This verse teaches us that every detail of worship is significant and should be done with care. As believers, we are called to offer God the best of ourselves, whether in our worship, actions, or service. This prompts us to reflect on how we honor God in our daily lives.

mots.sens: This word means 'wise' or 'skilled'. It evokes practical and intellectual competence, often associated with the ability to understand and apply knowledge in concrete situations. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the importance of wisdom and skill in carrying out divine commands, reminding us that God calls individuals with specific talents to accomplish His work.

This term means 'to do' or 'to execute'. It is often used in the Bible to describe the action of creating or accomplishing something according to God's will. In this verse, it highlights the importance of concrete action and obedience to divine will, emphasizing that faith must be translated into tangible acts.

This word is a particle that introduces the direct object of a verb. Although it is often considered grammatical, its presence in the text underscores the importance of what follows, namely the commands of the Lord. It reminds us that every detail of God's will deserves our attention and commitment.

This sacred name of God, often translated as 'the Lord', represents divine covenant and faithfulness. It evokes the immutable and sovereign nature of God, who calls His people to respond to His instructions. In this verse, it emphasizes that the commands given are not merely suggestions, but commandments from the Creator.

10.epoque: This verse is located in the book of Exodus, which recounts the story of the people of Israel during their exodus from Egypt, around the 13th century B.C. It is a period of formation and revelation of Israel's national and spiritual identity under the leadership of Moses.
10.passage: Exodus 35 is part of the instructions given by God regarding the construction of the tabernacle, a place of meeting between God and His people. This chapter emphasizes the importance of each member of the community's contribution to God's work.
10.culture: In Israelite culture, craftsmanship and manual skills were valued, and each individual was seen as having a unique role to play in the community. This reflects a collective understanding of the importance of personal commitment in serving God.
10.interpretation: This verse reminds us that God calls each of us to use our talents and skills in service of His work. It is not just about those who are qualified by society, but about all who are willing to obey and act according to His will.
10.commentaire: The call to those who have skill is an invitation to recognize and use the gifts that God has given us. As believers, we are called to respond to God's invitation by actively engaging in His work, whether in the church or in our daily lives. Every act of obedience and service counts in the divine plan.

mots.sens: This term refers to the 'tabernacle', which is the place of divine presence among the people of Israel. It comes from the root 'שָׁכַן' (shakan), which means 'to dwell' or 'to reside'. Theologically, the Mishkan symbolizes God's dwelling in the midst of His people, highlighting the intimacy of the relationship between God and humanity.

This word means 'tent', and it evokes a temporary structure, symbolizing the provisional nature of earthly life. The tent is a place of refuge and protection, also representing the mobility of the people of Israel in the desert. Spiritually, this reminds us that our earthly dwelling is temporary and that our true home is in heaven.

This term translates to 'covering' and refers to what protects and preserves. In the context of the tabernacle, the covering symbolizes divine protection over the people. It also reminds us that God is our refuge and protection in times of vulnerability.

This word means 'column', and it represents an essential supporting structure. The columns of the tabernacle support the tent, symbolizing the strength and stability of God's presence. Theologically, this teaches us that our faith must be founded on the solidity of divine truth.

11.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, freed from slavery in Egypt, receive precise instructions to build a place of worship in the midst of the desert.
11.passage: In Exodus 35, the people are called to contribute to the construction of the tabernacle, which is the symbol of God's presence among them. This chapter emphasizes the importance of obedience and community participation in worship.
11.culture: In the nomadic culture of the Israelites, the tabernacle was an essential structure that provided a place of meeting with God, while being mobile to adapt to their way of life. This also reflects the practices of neighboring peoples who built portable sanctuaries.
11.interpretation: The tabernacle, with all its elements, represents how God desires to be present and accessible to His people. Each component has a spiritual significance that reminds us that our worship must be centered on God's presence in our lives.
11.commentaire: This verse invites us to reflect on our own spiritual 'tabernacle'. Just as the people of Israel were called to contribute to the construction of the tabernacle, we are also called to invest our time, talents, and resources to build our faith community. By recognizing God's presence among us, we must live in accordance with this reality, seeking to honor God in all that we do.

mots.sens: This word refers to the ark of the covenant, a sacred chest that contained the tablets of the law. It is derived from the Hebrew root 'א-ר-ן' which evokes the idea of protection and preservation. Theologically, the ark symbolizes God's presence among His people and the link between the divine and humanity, thus representing Christ as the mediator of the new covenant.

This term refers to the mercy seat, the cover of the ark, where the blood of sacrifices was sprinkled for the atonement of sins. It is related to the root 'כ-פ-ר' which means 'to cover' or 'atonement'. Spiritually, the mercy seat represents God's mercy and the means by which sins are covered, foreshadowing the sacrifice of Christ that brings redemption.

This word means 'to cover' and is used here to describe the veil that separated the Holy of Holies from the rest of the tabernacle. It comes from the root 'ס-כ-ך' which implies a notion of protection or shelter. Theologically, this veil symbolizes the separation between God and man due to sin, and its tearing at the crucifixion of Christ opens direct access to the presence of God.

12.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, freed from slavery in Egypt, receive precise instructions on the construction of the tabernacle during their journey in the desert.
12.passage: Exodus 35 describes the contributions of the Israelites for the construction of the tabernacle and the sacred objects that will be placed there, highlighting the importance of God's presence among His people.
12.culture: In Hebrew culture, the tabernacle was the center of religious and communal life, representing the meeting between God and His people. Sacred objects, such as the ark and the mercy seat, were considered extremely holy.
12.interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sacred objects in Israelite worship, each having a deep and symbolic meaning. The ark, the mercy seat, and the veil illustrate the relationship between God and humanity, as well as the need for atonement to access divine holiness.
12.commentaire: The ark and its elements remind us that God desires to dwell among His people and that holiness is essential in our relationship with Him. As Christians, we must recognize that, through the sacrifice of Christ, we have direct access to God's presence, and this should motivate us to live in accordance with His will, seeking to honor His holiness in our daily lives.

mots.sens: This word means 'table' and specifically refers to the table used in the tabernacle to present the showbread. It is derived from the root 'שָׁלַח' which means 'to send' or 'to extend', evoking the idea of offering or sharing. Theologically, the table represents communion and divine provision, emphasizing that God provides for our spiritual needs.

This term means 'bars' and refers to the bars that support the table in the tabernacle. These bars, as structural elements, symbolize the stability and strength of God's presence among His people. Spiritually, they remind us that our faith is supported by the strength of God, who keeps us firm in our trials.

The word 'bread' refers here to the showbread, which was offered as a sign of communion with God. Bread is a fundamental symbol of life and sustenance, also representing Christ, the 'bread of life' (John 6:35). In this context, it emphasizes the idea that God nourishes His people spiritually and physically.

13.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, after their departure from Egypt, receive specific instructions for the construction of the tabernacle, a symbol of God's presence among them.
13.passage: Exodus 35 discusses the contributions of the Israelites for the construction of the tabernacle and its utensils, highlighting the importance of community participation in worship and devotion to God.
13.culture: In Hebrew culture, the table and the offerings of bread were central elements of worship, representing hospitality and communion with God. The showbread also served as a reminder of divine provision in the wilderness.
13.interpretation: This verse reminds us that God desires to establish a relationship of communion with His people, symbolized by the table and the showbread. He invites us to recognize His presence and provision in our lives while committing ourselves to offer Him our devotion.
13.commentaire: The mention of the table and its utensils teaches us the importance of preparation and consecration in our worship. Just as the Israelites were called to bring their contributions for the tabernacle, we are also called to offer our lives and resources to God. By recognizing His provision, we can live in gratitude and communion with Him, knowing that He is the true bread of life that satisfies our souls.

mots.sens: The word 'menorah' refers to a seven-branched lampstand, a symbol of divine light. It comes from the Hebrew root 'נור' (nur), which means 'light' or 'flame'. In a theological context, the menorah represents God's presence among His people and the spiritual illumination He brings. It is also a symbol of wisdom and knowledge, essential for walking in God's ways.

The term 'shemen' means 'oil' and is often associated with anointing and consecration. It is derived from the root 'שמן' (shaman) which evokes the idea of abundance and richness. Spiritually, oil symbolizes the Holy Spirit, who provides strength and illumination to believers. In the context of the lampstand, oil is essential for fueling the light, illustrating the necessity of divine presence in the lives of the faithful.

The word 'keli' means 'utensil' or 'instrument', and refers to any object used in the service of God. It is derived from the root 'כל' (kal), which means 'all' or 'complete'. In the context of worship, utensils are instruments of sanctification, allowing believers to approach God. Each 'keli' has a specific function, highlighting the importance of each element in worship and relationship with the Creator.

14.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, recently freed from slavery in Egypt, receive specific instructions from God for the construction of the Tabernacle.
14.passage: Exodus 35 discusses the collection of materials needed for the Tabernacle and the making of the sacred objects that will be used there, highlighting the importance of community commitment in worship.
14.culture: In Israelite culture, worship was centered on material objects, all of which had deep spiritual significance. Light, in particular, was a symbol of divine presence and guidance.
14.interpretation: The lampstand and its utensils represent not only physical light but also the spiritual light that God brings to His people. Oil, as a symbol of the Holy Spirit, reminds believers of the necessity to be filled with God's presence to shine in the world.
14.commentaire: This verse reminds us of the importance of light in our spiritual lives. Just as the lampstand required oil to illuminate, we need the Holy Spirit to light our path. As believers, we are called to be bright witnesses in our environment, reflecting God's glory through our actions and words.

mots.sens: The word 'mizbeach' means 'altar' and derives from the root 'zavach', which means 'to sacrifice'. In the biblical context, the altar is a place of encounter with God, where sacrifices are offered for the atonement of sins. Spiritually, it symbolizes the necessity of mediation between man and God, and reminds us of the importance of worship and consecration in our Christian life.

The term 'shemen' means 'oil' and evokes the idea of consecration and sanctification. In the Bible, oil is often used to signify the Holy Spirit and divine presence. Anointing oil is a symbol of divine election, marking people or objects as set apart for sacred service.

The word 'ketoret' refers to 'incense', which is used in worship to create an atmosphere of holiness. Incense is a symbol of prayer and worship, representing the prayers of the saints ascending to God. It emphasizes the importance of sincere worship and communion with the Lord.

The word 'sader' means 'curtain' and refers to the separation between the sacred and the profane. The curtain of the tabernacle door symbolizes access to God's presence while indicating the necessity of purification to approach Him. Theologically, it evokes the sacrifice of Christ, who opened the way to the Holy of Holies.

15.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the people of Israel during their journey in the desert, after the Exodus from Egypt, and before entering the Promised Land.
15.passage: Exodus 35 describes the instructions given by Moses for the construction of the tabernacle and sacred objects, highlighting the importance of worship and service to God.
15.culture: In Israelite culture, sacred objects, such as the altar and anointing oil, were essential for worship and relationship with God, reflecting a community life centered on spirituality.
15.interpretation: This verse emphasizes the need to consecrate places and objects for divine service, while reminding us that worship must be done with pure hearts and sincere intentions. It invites us to reflect on our own devotion and commitment to God.
15.commentaire: The altar of incense and the other elements mentioned in this verse remind us of the importance of worship in our Christian life. Just as these objects were essential for worship in the tabernacle, our worship must be centered on Christ, who is our mediator. Let us commit to dedicating our lives to God, offering our prayers and actions as a pleasing aroma in His sight.

mots.sens: The word 'mizbeach' refers to an altar, a place of sacrifice. It comes from the root 'zavach', which means 'to sacrifice'. In the biblical context, the altar is a symbol of intercession and redemption, representing the place where man meets God through sacrifice. Theologically, this reminds us that Christ, as our ultimate altar, offered the perfect sacrifice for our sins.

The term 'kiyor' translates to 'basin' and refers to a vessel used for ritual purification. It is related to the idea of purification and sanctification, essential in ancient worship. In a spiritual sense, this represents the need for inner purification, foreshadowing the washing we receive through the word of God and the blood of Christ.

The word 'barzel' means 'bronze', a metal often used in the making of sacred utensils. It evokes solidity and durability, symbolizing the strength and resilience of divine ordinances. In a spiritual context, this can remind us that God's truths are eternal and that our faith must be anchored in solid foundations.

16.epoque: This verse is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites received instructions to build the tabernacle after their departure from Egypt, marking a time of formation and establishment of divine law.
16.passage: In Exodus 35, the people are called to contribute to the construction of the tabernacle and its utensils, highlighting the importance of collective participation in the worship of God and the establishment of His dwelling among them.
16.culture: In ancient Israelite culture, sacrifices and purification rituals were central to religious life, reflecting a deep understanding of the holiness of God and the need for reconciliation between man and the Creator.
16.interpretation: The altar of burnt offerings and the basin with its base represent essential elements of worship, symbolizing the necessity of sacrifice and purification to draw near to God. Spiritually, this reminds us that our approach to God must be made with a pure heart and a repentant spirit.
16.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of spiritual preparation in our worship. Just as the Israelites had to prepare the utensils for worship, we too must prepare ourselves inwardly to meet God, submitting to His purification through prayer and repentance. In Christ, we have access to this purification and direct communion with God.

mots.sens: This term primarily refers to a tent or shelter. In the context of the Tabernacle, it represents the presence of God among His people. The word 'ohel' also evokes the idea of protection and intimacy, emphasizing God's desire to draw near to His people while providing them with a sacred place for worship.

This word means 'column' and refers to a pillar supporting a structure. In the context of the Tabernacle, the columns symbolize the stability and strength of the divine presence. Spiritually, they also represent the support that God offers to His people, enabling them to stand firm in faith.

This term refers to the base or pedestal on which a structure rests. In the context of the Tabernacle, the bases of the columns are essential for ensuring the solidity of the edifice. Theologically, this can symbolize the foundation of faith, where Christ is the base upon which we build our spiritual lives.

This word means 'dwelling' or 'habitation', and it is often used to refer to the Tabernacle. It represents the place where God dwells among His people. Spiritually, 'mishkan' emphasizes the idea of communion and divine presence, reminding believers that God desires to establish an intimate relationship with them.

17.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, freed from slavery in Egypt, receive instructions to build the Tabernacle, a place of meeting with God.
17.passage: Exodus 35 describes the contributions and materials needed for the construction of the Tabernacle, highlighting the importance of obedience and the people's commitment to God's commandments.
17.culture: In Israelite culture, the Tabernacle was a central symbol of God's presence and community. The materials used for its construction held great value, representing the people's devotion to their God.
17.interpretation: This verse reminds us that each element of the Tabernacle has a profound spiritual significance. The fabrics, columns, and curtains are symbols of the separation between the sacred and the profane, while affirming God's closeness to His people.
17.commentaire: The passage teaches us the importance of contributing to God's work with our resources and time. By building the Tabernacle, the Israelites demonstrate their commitment to God, inviting us to reflect on our own devotion and willingness to serve in the divine work.

mots.sens: This term refers to 'pegs' or 'supports', serving to establish solid structures. In the context of the tabernacle, these pegs symbolize the stability and security of the divine presence among His people. Spiritually, they evoke the necessity of a solid foundation in our faith, anchored in the truth of God.

This word means 'garment' or 'utensil', and in this context, it refers to the priestly garments intended for service. These garments are not only functional elements but also symbols of holiness and service before God. Theologically, this underscores the importance of preparation and purity in divine service.

This term translates to 'courtyard' and alludes to the outer space of the tabernacle, a place of gathering and worship. The courtyard represents access to the presence of God while delineating a sacred space. This reminds us that, although God is accessible, there is an appropriate way to approach Him.

18.epoque: This passage is set during the Israelites' wandering in the desert, after their departure from Egypt, as they receive instructions to build the tabernacle as a place of meeting with God.
18.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses reminds the people of the divine instructions regarding the construction of the tabernacle and the elements necessary for its service, emphasizing the importance of community participation in God's work.
18.culture: In Israelite culture, the tabernacle was the center of spiritual and communal life, representing the tangible presence of God among His people. The construction of the tabernacle involved contributions from all, highlighting the importance of collective commitment in worship.
18.interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of material elements in worship, which are reflections of spiritual reality. The pegs and priestly garments symbolize both the structure of worship and the preparation required to enter into God's presence.
18.commentaire: The passage teaches us that every detail in our service to God is significant. Just as the Israelites were called to contribute to the construction of the tabernacle, we are also called to invest our resources and talents to build the Church. This reminds us that our commitment to divine service must be made with care and devotion, reflecting our desire to glorify God in all that we do.

mots.sens: This term means 'clothes' and specifically refers to the garments worn by the priests. In the biblical context, sacred clothing is not only an element of adornment but also symbolizes holiness and separation for the service of God. They are designed to reflect divine glory and the authority of the priesthood, thus emphasizing the necessity of spiritual preparation for those who approach God.

This word designates a 'priest' or 'sacrificer', a person consecrated to serve in divine worship. Priests are intermediaries between God and the people, and their role is essential in the fulfillment of sacred rites. In this verse, Aaron and his sons represent the first priesthood instituted by God, highlighting the importance of lineage and consecration in divine service.

This term means 'sacred' or 'holy', and it is often used to describe what is set apart for God. In the context of clothing, this indicates that these garments are not ordinary but dedicated for divine use. The holiness of the garments underscores the necessity of inner and outer purity for those who present themselves before God.

19.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites left Egypt and received instructions on the construction of the Tabernacle and the worship to be rendered to God.
19.passage: Exodus 35 is part of the instructions given to Moses regarding contributions for the Tabernacle and the sacred garments, emphasizing the importance of preparation for divine service.
19.culture: In Israelite culture, clothing had a profound significance, representing not only social status but also spiritual function. The garments of the priests were a symbol of their sacred role and their separation for the service of God.
19.interpretation: The verse emphasizes the importance of preparation and consecration in the service of God. Sacred garments are not merely clothing but symbols of the relationship between God and His people, reminding that those who serve must be purified and dedicated to their mission.
19.commentaire: This passage reminds us that serving God requires serious preparation and consecration. Just as the priests of the Old Testament had to wear sacred garments, we too, as believers, are called to put on 'the armor of God' to fulfill our ministry. This invites us to reflect on our own lives and ensure that we are ready to serve with purity and devotion.

mots.sens: This word designates the concept of assembly or community. It evokes the idea of a group united by a common cause, here that of obedience to God. In the spiritual context, this underscores the importance of communion among believers and their collective commitment to divine instructions.

This verb means 'to go out' or 'to exit'. It implies a physical movement but also a spiritual one, symbolizing a transition from one state to another. In the passage, this may represent the Israelites' response to Moses' call, highlighting their willingness to leave the presence of God to put His commandments into practice.

Moses is the leader chosen by God to guide the people of Israel. His name means 'drawn out of the waters', symbolizing his role as a deliverer. In this verse, he represents divine authority and mediation between God and His people, which is fundamental in the relationship between humanity and the divine.

This term refers to the assembly or congregation. It emphasizes the idea of a gathering of people for a common purpose, often related to worship or adoration. Spiritually, this reminds us that the people of God are called to come together to worship and serve collectively.

20.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, recently freed from slavery in Egypt, receive instructions on the construction of the Tabernacle.
20.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses reminds the people of God's commandments regarding the construction of the Tabernacle, a place of meeting with God. This verse marks the collective response of the people to this divine call.
20.culture: In Israelite culture, the assembly was essential for worship and community life. The active participation of each member was expected for the fulfillment of God's projects.
20.interpretation: This verse illustrates the people's response to Moses' authority, representing the voice of God. Their exit from Moses' presence symbolizes a step toward action, where they are called to put divine instructions into practice.
20.commentaire: This passage reminds us of the importance of collective obedience to God's call. As a community of believers, we are called to step out of our comfort zone to serve and honor God together. This encourages us to actively respond to divine instructions in our daily lives.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to give voluntarily' or 'to offer generously'. It evokes the idea of an offering made willingly, without compulsion. In this verse, it emphasizes the importance of inner motivation in the act of giving, which is essential in serving God.

The word 'heart' designates not only the physical organ but also the seat of emotions, thoughts, and intentions. In the biblical context, the heart is often considered the center of human will. This shows that the offering to the Lord must come from a sincere and committed inner disposition.

This term means 'dwelling' or 'habitation', and refers to the tent of meeting, the place where God resides among His people. It symbolizes divine presence and the link between God and Israel. The work of the tent of meeting is therefore essential for worship and communion with God.

This word designates a 'raised offering' or 'contribution'. It is often used to describe gifts made to God for sacred works. In the context of this verse, it underscores the importance of giving for the work of God, recognizing His greatness and participating in His plan.

21.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, as Israel is on its way to the Promised Land, having received God's law at Sinai.
21.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses calls the people to contribute to the construction of the tabernacle, a place of meeting between God and His people. This chapter highlights the importance of willingness and personal commitment in serving God.
21.culture: In Israelite culture, offerings were a way to show devotion and commitment to God. Contributions for the tabernacle were seen as an act of participation in community and spiritual life.
21.interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God seeks willing and generous hearts to serve His work. The offering is not only material but must also reflect an attitude of faith and gratitude toward God.
21.commentaire: This passage reminds us that our service to God must be motivated by a sincere heart and a willingness to give. As Christians, we are called to contribute not only with our resources but also with our time and talents, recognizing that all we have comes from God. May our commitment to God's work be an act of praise and devotion.

mots.sens: This word means 'good' or 'well-disposed.' It evokes a favorable inner disposition, a willingness to serve and give. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the importance of a heart attitude in the offering, indicating that God seeks sincere and generous hearts to accomplish His work.

This term refers to an offering or gift, often associated with an act of devotion. It represents not only a material act but also a spiritual commitment to God. In this verse, it highlights that offerings are a means of dedicating what one has to the Lord, thereby manifesting a recognition of His provision.

This word means 'gold,' symbolizing value and wealth. In biblical culture, gold is often associated with glory and divine presence. The offering of gold here demonstrates that believers are willing to give what they consider precious to honor God, illustrating the spiritual priority over material goods.

22.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, where the people of Israel, recently freed from slavery, are receiving instructions for the construction of the Tabernacle, a place of meeting with God.
22.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses calls the people to contribute to the construction of the Tabernacle. This chapter highlights the generosity and commitment of the Israelites, both men and women, in God's work.
22.culture: In Israelite culture, offerings were an act of devotion and recognition toward God. They were often seen as a way to participate in the divine work and to show one's commitment to the community and faith.
22.interpretation: This verse illustrates that the offering to God does not depend on material wealth, but on the disposition of the heart. Each individual, regardless of status, is called to contribute according to their ability and willingness, reflecting equality before God.
22.commentaire: This passage reminds us that God desires not only material offerings but also well-disposed hearts. As believers, we are called to give not only of our possessions but also of our time and talents, ensuring that our attitude is one of sincere devotion. Let us reflect on how we can dedicate our resources to God's work in our community.

mots.sens: This word refers to a blue color, often associated with royalty and divinity in Israelite tradition. Blue is also a symbol of divine revelation and faithfulness. In the context of the tabernacle, this color reminds us of God's presence and the importance of holiness in worship.

The argaman is a purple dye, obtained from a mollusk, and symbolizes wealth and majesty. In the Bible, this color is often associated with royalty and dignity. Spiritually, it evokes the sacrifice of Christ, who is the King of kings, and the importance of nobility in our service to God.

Fine linen is a high-quality fabric, often used in priestly garments. It symbolizes purity and holiness, and in the biblical context, it is often associated with justice and righteousness. This reminds us that our service to God should be done with a pure heart and a righteous life.

This term refers to skin, often used for making tents and other items. In the context of the tabernacle, the skins of rams and dolphins represent the protection and covering that God offers to His people. Spiritually, this evokes the necessity of being clothed in grace and divine protection in our walk with Him.

23.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, having come out of Egypt, receive instructions to build the tabernacle, a symbol of God's presence among them.
23.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses calls the people to contribute the materials necessary for the tabernacle, emphasizing the importance of collective participation in worship and service to God.
23.culture: In Israelite culture, offerings of precious materials for the tabernacle were an act of devotion and recognition of God's goodness. This reflects a tradition of generosity and community commitment.
23.interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of personal contribution in worship and service to God. Each item brought represents not only a material gift but also an act of faith and devotion toward the Lord.
23.commentaire: This passage teaches us that God desires our active participation in His work. By bringing our talents, resources, and time, we contribute to the building of His kingdom. Let us reflect on how we can offer our lives and goods for the glory of God and the service of others.

mots.sens: This term refers to an offering, often a gift made to God, which can include material elements such as agricultural products or precious items. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the act of devotion and recognition toward the Lord by bringing goods that will serve in the construction of the tabernacle. Spiritually, this represents our commitment to give of our time, resources, and hearts in service to God.

This word refers to brass or bronze, a metal used in the making of sacred objects and instruments of worship. Brass symbolizes strength and durability, and in this passage, it is associated with the idea of contributing to God's work with valuable materials. Spiritually, this reminds us that our gifts should be of quality and reflect our devotion to God.

This term refers to acacia wood, a valuable and durable material used for the construction of the tabernacle. Acacia wood is often associated with resilience and longevity, symbolizing the solidity of God's presence among His people. Spiritually, this invites us to offer what is precious and enduring in our lives to God for His service.

24.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, a time when the Israelites, recently freed from slavery in Egypt, are preparing to establish their worship and relationship with God in the wilderness.
24.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses calls the people to contribute to the construction of the tabernacle, a meeting place between God and His people. This chapter highlights the generosity and commitment of the Israelites to divine service.
24.culture: In Israelite culture, offerings were an act of devotion and recognition toward God. They were seen as a way to actively participate in the divine work, thereby strengthening the community and the relationship with the Lord.
24.interpretation: This verse illustrates the importance of voluntary contribution and personal commitment in the service of God. Each gift, whether material or spiritual, is precious and necessary for the advancement of God's kingdom.
24.commentaire: This passage teaches us that our commitment to God must translate into concrete actions. By bringing our resources, we participate in the divine work and testify to our faith. Let us reflect on what we can offer to God, not only of our material goods but also of our time and talents, to serve His cause.

mots.sens: This word means 'wisdom' or 'skill.' It evokes not only intellectual ability but also practical competence in arts and crafts. In this context, it emphasizes that women bring their expertise to contribute to God's work, showing that every gift and talent is valuable in divine service.

This term designates a specific 'blue,' often associated with royalty and divinity. The color blue has a deep spiritual significance, representing the sky and the presence of God. In the context of the tabernacle, it symbolizes holiness and divine connection, reminding the Israelites of their calling to be a holy people.

This word means 'fine linen,' a precious and high-quality material. Linen is often associated with purity and beauty, and its use in the tabernacle underscores the importance of quality in serving God. Spiritually, it reminds us that God deserves the best of our efforts and resources.

25.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, recently freed from slavery in Egypt, receive instructions to build the tabernacle, a place of meeting between God and His people.
25.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses calls the people to contribute to the construction of the tabernacle. This chapter highlights the importance of community engagement and the use of individual gifts to honor God.
25.culture: In Israelite culture, manual labor and craftsmanship were valued. Women, in particular, played a key role in passing on skills and traditions, and their contribution to the tabernacle was essential for the spiritual life of the community.
25.interpretation: This verse illustrates that everyone, regardless of status, can contribute to God's work. Women, through their skill, show that both spiritual and material gifts are necessary to build God's house.
25.commentaire: This passage reminds us that God calls each of us to use our talents and skills for His glory. Like these women, we are invited to bring our unique contribution to God's work, whether it be our time, resources, or talents. By serving diligently and passionately, we participate in the building of His kingdom on earth.

mots.sens: This word means 'women' and specifically refers to adult women. In the biblical context, it often represents figures of faith and devotion. Their involvement in sacred tasks, such as making materials for the tabernacle, underscores their active role in the community and their ability to contribute to divine service.

The term 'heart' evokes the seat of emotions, thoughts, and intentions. In the Bible, the heart is often associated with will and spiritual motivation. Here, it indicates that the commitment of the women is not just a matter of skill but also of inner disposition and devotion to God.

This word means 'wisdom' or 'skill' and implies practical competence as well as spiritual understanding. In the context of building the tabernacle, it emphasizes the importance of divine wisdom in carrying out sacred tasks. It reminds us that God equips His people with gifts to serve in His work.

This term means 'to spin' or 'to work with materials.' It implies a creative and meticulous process, essential for making the elements of the tabernacle. It underscores the importance of manual labor and craftsmanship in worship, and by extension, in the Christian life where every act can be an act of praise.

26.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, recently freed from slavery in Egypt, receive precise instructions to build the tabernacle, a symbol of God's presence among them.
26.passage: Exodus 35 addresses the contribution of the Israelites to the construction of the tabernacle. This verse highlights the role of women in this work, emphasizing that their hearts and skills were essential to fulfill God's will.
26.culture: In the Israelite culture of the time, manual labor and craftsmanship were valued, and every member of the community, including women, had a role to play in serving God. The contribution of women in spiritual tasks was recognized and respected.
26.interpretation: This verse teaches us that God calls everyone, regardless of gender, to contribute to His work with a willing heart. The inner disposition and talents given by God are essential to fulfill His will on earth.
26.commentaire: This passage encourages us to be attentive to our own hearts and our willingness to serve. Like these women, we are called to use our gifts and skills to contribute to God's work in our communities. Every act of service, whether great or small, can have an eternal impact when done with love and devotion.

mots.sens: The word 'onyx' designates a precious stone, often used in ornaments and priestly garments. In the context of the ephod and the breastplate, onyx symbolizes the beauty and value of sacred things, representing the presence of God among His people. Spiritually, it reminds us of the importance of worship and dignity in serving God.

The term 'hashuv' means 'principal' or 'important,' indicating a position of leadership or authority. In this verse, it highlights the role of the leaders of the people in bringing materials for the tabernacle, showing their commitment to God's service. It also evokes the idea that those in positions of responsibility must actively contribute to God's work.

The ephod is a priestly garment worn by the high priest, symbolizing ministry and intercession before God. It is a central element in worship, representing mediation between God and His people. Theologically, the ephod reminds us that divine service requires sacred and precious elements, emphasizing the importance of holiness in worship.

The breastplate, or 'choshen,' is another priestly garment that contains the twelve stones representing the tribes of Israel. It symbolizes the representation of the people before God and the importance of each tribe in the divine plan. Spiritually, it reminds us that every believer has a place and value in the kingdom of God.

27.epoque: This verse is set in the context of the Exodus, after the exodus from Egypt, when God gives precise instructions for the construction of the tabernacle and sacred objects. It is a period of identity formation for the people of Israel, who are learning to worship the living God.
27.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses calls the people to contribute to the construction of the tabernacle, a meeting place between God and His people. This chapter emphasizes the importance of collective participation and commitment in serving God.
27.culture: In ancient Israelite culture, precious stones had great symbolic and material value. They were often associated with royalty and holiness, and their use in worship underscores the importance of beauty and value in divine service.
27.interpretation: This verse shows that serving God requires valuable and meaningful contributions. The leaders of the people, by bringing stones for the ephod and the breastplate, demonstrate their dedication and desire to see God's presence among them. This invites us to reflect on our own commitment to God's work.
27.commentaire: The contribution of stones by the leaders of the people illustrates the importance of active participation of believers in God's service. Each of us is called to bring what we have of value for the work of the Lord. Let us reflect on how we can contribute to the advancement of God's kingdom in our lives and in our community.

mots.sens: This word means 'oil' and generally refers to a fatty substance used for anointing, lighting, and offerings. In the biblical context, oil symbolizes the presence of the Holy Spirit and divine anointing. It is often associated with consecration and purification, highlighting the importance of separation for the service of God.

This term translates to 'spices' and refers to fragrant substances used in religious rites and offerings. The spices symbolize prayer and worship, representing the elevation of hearts toward God. In the context of worship, they remind us that our worship must be pleasing and fragrant in the eyes of God.

This word means 'offering' and generally refers to a contribution made to God, often in the form of food or valuable items. In the context of sacrifices, it represents the act of devotion and gratitude toward God. Spiritually, it reminds us that everything we have comes from Him and that we must offer Him the best of ourselves.

28.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the people of Israel are on their way to the Promised Land after being freed from slavery in Egypt. It is a time of formation and establishment of the laws and rituals that will govern their communal and spiritual life.
28.passage: Exodus 35 addresses the instructions given by Moses regarding the construction of the Tabernacle and sacred objects. This chapter emphasizes the importance of the voluntary contribution of the people for the realization of these holy works.
28.culture: In Israelite culture, spices and oil had a profound significance, often associated with rituals of purification and worship. The use of these elements in worship shows the value placed on beauty and quality in the service of God.
28.interpretation: Spiritually, this verse reminds us that our worship must be accompanied by precious gifts, representing our commitment and devotion to God. Oil and spices symbolize the presence of the Holy Spirit that sanctifies our offerings and our worship.
28.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of giving our best to God, whether through our material resources or our time. By offering what is precious, we acknowledge His sovereignty and goodness in our lives. May our worship be like a pleasing aroma, attracting God's presence among us.

mots.sens: This word means 'to give voluntarily' or 'to offer willingly'. It is derived from the root that evokes the idea of generosity and the disposition of the heart. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the importance of inner motivation to contribute to God's work, indicating that the offering is not merely an external act, but a reflection of a spiritual attitude. Theologically, it reminds us that God desires willing hearts to serve and give, rather than forced sacrifices.

This term means 'heart' and represents the center of human emotions, thoughts, and wills. In the Bible, the heart is often seen as the seat of the personal relationship with God. In this verse, it emphasizes that the disposition of the heart is essential for an authentic contribution to the work of the Lord, reminding us that God looks beyond outward actions to discern the inner attitude.

This word translates to 'offering' or 'gift', and it is often associated with contributions made for sacred causes. It evokes the idea of giving something of value to serve God's purposes. In this context, it emphasizes the importance of personal commitment in the divine work, showing that every contribution, even small, is precious in God's eyes.

This name, which means 'drawn out of the waters', refers to Moses, the leader chosen by God to free Israel from slavery. Moses is a central figure in the history of Israel and a mediator of divine law. In this verse, his role as God's spokesperson underscores the divine authority behind the call to offer, reminding us that contributing to God's work is a response to His command.

29.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, recently freed from slavery in Egypt, are on their way to the Promised Land under Moses' leadership.
29.passage: Exodus chapter 35 deals with the preparation of the tabernacle, a meeting place between God and His people. This verse highlights the Israelites' response to God's call to contribute to the construction of this sacred space.
29.culture: In Israelite culture, offerings were a way to demonstrate devotion to God and actively participate in community life. Generosity was valued and seen as an act of faith.
29.interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of the disposition of the heart in serving God. It teaches us that contributions should be made willingly and joyfully, reflecting an authentic relationship with the Lord.
29.commentaire: This passage reminds us that God seeks willing hearts to give for His work. As believers, we are called to examine our motivations and offer our resources, whether material or spiritual, with an attitude of gratitude and devotion. Every act of generosity, even the humblest, has eternal value in God's eyes.

mots.sens: The name Betsaleel means 'under the shadow of God', which evokes divine closeness and protection. This name emphasizes the idea that talents and skills are given by God and should be used for His glory. In the context of the construction of the tabernacle, it reminds us that every work for God must be inspired by His presence and direction.

This term means 'God' and is often used to denote divine power and authority. In this verse, it emphasizes God's choice of Betsaleel, showing that it is God who equips and calls those He has chosen for His mission. This reminds us that our calling and gifts come from God and should be recognized as such.

This word means 'to send' or 'to choose', and it is often used in the context of divine mission. In this passage, it indicates that God specifically chose Betsaleel for an important task, highlighting the significance of divine calling in the lives of believers. It teaches us that every Christian has a unique role in God's plan.

30.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, recently freed from slavery in Egypt, receive specific instructions for the construction of the tabernacle. It is a period of identity formation for the people of God.
30.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses reminds the people of the importance of obedience to God's commandments, particularly regarding the construction of the tabernacle. This chapter highlights the role of Betsaleel as the chosen craftsman to carry out this sacred work.
30.culture: In Israelite culture, craftsmanship and construction were highly respected activities, often seen as divine gifts. The construction of the tabernacle was not only a physical task but also an act of devotion and worship toward God.
30.interpretation: This verse emphasizes that God chooses and equips specific individuals for specific tasks in His work. Betsaleel, as a craftsman, represents all those who are called to use their talents to serve God and His community.
30.commentaire: This passage reminds us that each of us has been chosen by God for a specific purpose. Like Betsaleel, we must recognize our gifts and use them to glorify God in our lives. It encourages us to seek God's direction in our daily activities and to work diligently for His glory.

mots.sens: This word means 'breath' or 'spirit'. In the biblical context, it evokes the life-giving presence of God. 'Ruach' is often associated with divine action, illustrating how God inspires and gives life to creation. In this verse, it emphasizes that it is by the Spirit of God that talents and abilities are granted for the work.

This term refers to wisdom, a deep and practical understanding of things. It is often linked to the ability to discern and apply knowledge in concrete situations. In the context of this verse, it shows that the wisdom given by God is essential for carrying out specific tasks, thus reflecting divine wisdom in human work.

This word means 'understanding' or 'insight'. It refers to the ability to comprehend things deeply and make informed judgments. In this verse, it illustrates how spiritual intelligence, given by God, enables the successful completion of complex projects and the achievement of divine objectives.

This term means 'work' or 'labor'. It designates any form of creative or productive activity, often in relation to serving God. In this verse, it emphasizes that the work performed by men, when inspired by the Spirit of God, is sacred and has eternal value.

31.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites are on their way to the Promised Land, under the leadership of Moses, after their liberation from slavery in Egypt.
31.passage: Exodus 35 deals with the preparation of the tabernacle and the sacred objects that will be placed there. This verse emphasizes that God equips artisans to carry out this work with excellence.
31.culture: In Hebrew culture, manual labor and craftsmanship were valued, seen as means to serve God and the community. Skills were often perceived as divine gifts.
31.interpretation: This verse reminds us that every talent or skill we possess comes from God and should be used for His glory. The Holy Spirit plays a crucial role in equipping believers for specific works.
31.commentaire: This passage teaches us that God equips each believer by His Spirit to accomplish works that honor His name. We must be open to the Spirit and use our gifts to serve others and contribute to the advancement of His kingdom on earth.

mots.sens: This term refers to an 'invention' or a 'concept', indicating a creative and intellectual capacity. It comes from the root 'חָשַׁב' which means 'to think' or 'to calculate'. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes that God has given Bezalel a special wisdom to design works of art and sacred objects, revealing how God empowers His servants for specific tasks in His work.

The word 'silver' refers to a precious metal, often used in transactions and valuable objects. In Hebrew culture, silver also symbolizes wealth and prosperity. In this verse, it highlights the importance of precious materials in the construction of the Tabernacle, representing the value that God places on His dwelling among His people.

This term means 'copper' or 'bronze', a metal used for its durability and strength. It is often associated with objects of worship and instruments in the service of God. In this context, bronze symbolizes strength and protection, reminding us that God equips His artisans to accomplish works that honor Him.

32.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites wander in the desert after their departure from Egypt, and as they prepare to construct the Tabernacle, a dwelling for the presence of God among them.
32.passage: Chapter 35 of Exodus describes the instructions given by Moses to the people regarding the collection of materials for the Tabernacle, as well as the selection of Bezalel and Oholiab as the main artisans, highlighting the importance of divine craftsmanship in worship.
32.culture: In Hebrew culture, craftsmanship was highly respected, and artisans were seen as individuals endowed with divinely inspired skills. The creation of sacred objects was not only a material task but also an act of devotion to God.
32.interpretation: This verse shows that God equips His servants with specific talents and skills to accomplish His will. It reminds us that every gift and skill we possess comes from God and should be used for His glory.
32.commentaire: This passage teaches us that God does not only ask for our obedience, but He also equips us for service. Each of us has unique gifts, and it is essential to recognize and use them for the advancement of His kingdom. By working with excellence in our respective fields, we honor God and testify to His greatness.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to work carefully' or 'to engrave'. It evokes the idea of creating or shaping something with precision and skill. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the importance of craftsmanship in the construction of the tabernacle, revealing that God values manual labor and craftsmanship as a means of honoring His presence. Spiritually, this reminds us that every task, even the simplest, can be an act of devotion to God.

This term means 'stone' and often refers to precious stones or building materials. In the context of the construction of the tabernacle, it symbolizes the solidity and durability of God's presence among His people. Theologically, the stones to be set represent believers, who are 'living stones' in God's spiritual temple, highlighting our role in His work.

This verb means 'to make' or 'to execute' and implies the idea of accomplishing a task or producing something. In this verse, it emphasizes the concrete action and commitment of the artisans to create the works of art for the tabernacle. This reminds us that our faith must translate into tangible actions that glorify God and serve our community.

This term translates to 'work' or 'labor' and refers to any form of work, especially in a sacred context. In Exodus 35, it is associated with the creation of the tabernacle, emphasizing that work can be an act of worship. Spiritually, this teaches us that every activity, when done with a devoted heart, can be considered a service to God.

33.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, having come out of Egypt, receive precise instructions to build the tabernacle, a place of meeting with God.
33.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses reminds the people of the importance of contributing to the construction of the tabernacle, highlighting the gifts and talents that each person can bring to glorify God.
33.culture: In Hebrew culture, craftsmanship and manual work were highly valued, seen as means to honor God and participate in His work. The artisan was respected for his skills and dedication.
33.interpretation: This verse teaches us that God calls each of us to use our gifts and talents for His glory. By working with excellence, we participate in God's work and testify to our faith through our actions.
33.commentaire: This passage reminds us that service to God is not limited to spiritual activities but also includes our daily work. By exercising our skills and putting our talents to the service of God and our community, we testify to our commitment to Him. May every work we accomplish be an expression of our worship and devotion.

mots.sens: This verb means 'to teach' and comes from the root 'lamad', which evokes the idea of learning and transmitting knowledge. In the biblical context, teaching is not just a transmission of information, but also a spiritual and moral formation. This underscores the importance of wisdom and understanding in community life and worship, showing that teaching is an essential divine gift for guiding God's people.

This name means 'tent of my father', and it evokes a connection with family and community. Oholiab, as the son of Ahisamac, represents not only a talented craftsman but also a member of a lineage that contributes to the construction of the tabernacle. This name emphasizes the importance of family and community relationships in serving God, indicating that every contribution is valuable in the divine work.

This term means 'works' or 'acts', and it refers to the concrete actions performed by individuals.
