In the context of the construction of the tabernacle, this implies that gifts and talents are put to use for a divine purpose. It reminds us that our service to God must be manifested through tangible actions, and that every act of service is an expression of our worship.

34.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, as the Israelites are on their way to the Promised Land, having received specific instructions from God to build the tabernacle.
34.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses calls the people together to remind them of the importance of contributing to the construction of the tabernacle, a place of meeting with God. The verse highlights the gift of teaching granted to Bezalel and Oholiab, essential for guiding the people in this work.
34.culture: In Israelite culture, teaching and the transmission of traditions were crucial for maintaining the identity and faith of the people. Artisans were respected for their craftsmanship, and their role was considered a sacred service.
34.interpretation: This verse teaches us that God equips His people with specific gifts for the fulfillment of His will. Teaching is essential not only for the physical construction of the tabernacle but also for spiritually edifying the people of God.
34.commentaire: This passage reminds us that each of us has a role to play in God's work, whether through teaching or other gifts. We are called to recognize and use our talents to serve the community and glorify God. By cultivating our gifts, we actively participate in the divine mission, thus contributing to the building up of the body of Christ.

mots.sens: This word means 'wisdom' or 'intelligence' and evokes a deep and practical understanding of things. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the idea that God has endowed certain men with exceptional ability to carry out works of art and craftsmanship. Divine wisdom is therefore essential for the execution of sacred tasks, showing that human creativity can be a reflection of divine creativity.

This term translates to 'work' or 'craft' and often refers to a work done with care and skill. In this passage, it refers to the artistic and craft activities related to the construction of the Tabernacle. This underscores the importance of craftsmanship in worship and how work can be an act of devotion to God.

This word means 'plan' or 'design', implying a thoughtful and intentional conception. It evokes the idea that the works carried out are not merely the result of chance, but stem from divine inspiration and careful planning. This reminds us that God is a God of order and structure, who inspires creativity for His glory.

This term means 'stones' and is often associated with solidity and permanence. In the context of the construction of the Tabernacle, it symbolizes the foundation upon which the place of meeting with God rests. Spiritually, this reminds us that our faith must be built on solid foundations, anchored in the truth of God's Word.

35.epoque: This passage is set in the context of the Exodus, when the Israelites, recently freed from slavery in Egypt, receive specific instructions for the construction of the Tabernacle, a symbol of God's presence among them.
35.passage: In Exodus 35, Moses reminds the people of the importance of each person's contribution to the construction of the Tabernacle. This verse emphasizes that God has equipped certain individuals with intelligence and specific skills to carry out sacred works of art.
35.culture: In ancient Israelite culture, craftsmanship and manual skills were highly valued, especially when used for the service of God. Artisans were seen as instruments of divine will, and their work was viewed as an act of worship.
35.interpretation: This verse teaches us that God equips His people with specific gifts to accomplish His will. Every talent and skill, whether artistic or technical, can be used to glorify God and serve the community.
35.commentaire: This passage reminds us that God is the source of all creativity and skill. As Christians, we are called to use our talents to serve the Lord and contribute to the building up of His Church. Whether through art, manual work, or any other form of expression, every act can become an act of praise when done with a heart devoted to God.
